# Studios as First-Class Graph Citizens

> Child of **The Library Graph** (Epic, P0), which owns nodes, edges and D10 — *"a studio hierarchy is two nodes and a preference, not one name"*. This spec owns what the application does with that hierarchy: how it is **validated**, how it is **populated**, and how it is **shown**.
## Why this exists
Studios became `EntityProfile` rows in Phase C — correctly, per C1, because they genuinely have a logo, links and an external identity. But nothing in the application treats them as anything more than a string:
- The **profile page** is the actor page. A studio displays gender, hair colour, birth date and career span, and displays nothing about the one relationship that is genuinely its own.
- `studio_parent` had **0 rows** when this was written. D10's hierarchy exists in the schema and nowhere in the data.
- There is **no batch tool** for studios, though there is one for actors and one for videos — and studios are a node kind with an edge kind of their own.
## Findings from reading the code, 2026-08-06
Three constraints were discovered during design and changed it. Recorded because each was an assumption worth checking rather than believing.
**F1 — There is no ****`StudioMetadataProvider`****.** `Plugin.swift` defines `ActorMetadataProvider` and `VideoMetadataProvider` only, so studio facts arrive *only* as a by-product of matching a video. The source does already answer `searchStudio(term:limit:)` — used today by `studioId(named:)` in the plugin repo — but there is no fetch-by-id returning parent, aliases, urls or logo. A real Match Studios needs a new protocol **and** private-plugin-repo work.
**F2 — ****`AssetGridView`**** combines sidebar selections with ****`allSatisfy`****. It ANDs.** So showing a network's whole family by inserting each descendant as a `.studio(name)` item asks for videos belonging to *every* studio at once, which is zero for any real family. A family view needs its own `.studioFamily` case.
**F3 — Two conditions were detectable and surfaced nowhere.** A studio string with no `video_studio` edge behind it, and `LibraryStore.studioEdgeDisagreements()`, which already existed and nothing called.
## Decisions
| # | Decision | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **Both tools, audit first.** Validate Studios needs no plugin work and establishes the true state before anything is built on it. Then Match Studios, then the profile page. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 2 | **The profile page comes last.** `studio_parent` is empty, so building it first produces a screen that is correct and blank for every studio in the library. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 3 | **The validator reports and routes; it never fixes.** Every repair already has a screen that does it carefully and asks the right question first. A validator that also repaired would be a second, less careful implementation of five existing tools. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 4 | ~~**Family-wide video listing is deferred.**~~ **Reversed 2026-08-06 by the operator:** *"From a graph perspective, a studio should show the videos from its imprints — the display should separate imprints like we have done for the series gallery."* Built via the `.studioFamily` case F2 predicted, presented as collapsible per-imprint sections rather than one merged list. | Built 2026-08-06 |
| 5 | **A disagreeing parent is reported, never overwritten.** If a studio already carries a different parent, that is a genuine conflict about the world, and the graph's standing rule is that it refuses to guess. Follows GraphSync, which reports rather than resolves. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
| 6 | **Studio batch policy mirrors the actor one, decision for decision** — one candidate or it queues, fills only, logo never unattended, ambiguous skipped on re-runs. Three batch screens that behave differently is three things to learn. | Decided 2026-08-06 |
## Part 1 — Validate Studios
An audit in **Find Problems**, whose footer already promises *"These report rather than change anything."* Nine checks, sorted defects-first then by size, each naming the screen that resolves it.
| Check | Certain? | Routes to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video carries two studios | defect | Fix Duplicate Studios |
| Two studios differ only by case or spacing | defect | Repair Tag Spelling |
| Studio string with no `video_studio` edge | defect | Connect the Graph |
| Edge disagrees with the tag | defect | Match Again |
| Network on record with no profile | defect | *none yet* |
| A studio inside itself | defect | *none yet* |
| Studio in use with no profile row | unfinished | Connect the Graph |
| Studio not confirmed against a source | unfinished | Match Studios |
| Studio profile no video uses | unfinished | Remove Orphaned Profiles |
Two implementation notes worth keeping:
- Spelling collisions fold through `StudioResolution.identity`, **not** `lowercased()`. The spellings that actually collide are the ones a source ran the spaces out of, so a case-only fold — what the tag audit does — misses the most common half.
- Two-studio videos are **excluded** from the missing-edge check. They have no edge *by design*, so counting them would report one defect twice and make the check impossible to clear while a conflict existed. `studioEdgeDisagreements()` excludes them for the same reason.
Single-library and disabled while federated, like Connect the Graph: half of what it checks is edges, and an edge cannot span two libraries.
## Part 2 — Match Studios
The direct analogue of Match Actors, and what actually populates `studio_parent` rather than waiting for every video to be re-matched.
Needs `StudioMetadataProvider` (`search(name:)` + `fetch(studioId:)` → a proposal carrying canonical name, aliases, parent name and id, urls, logo), plus the fetch-by-id in the private plugin repo. The parent fields have precedent: `VideoMetadataProposal` already carries `studioParent` and `studioParentSourceId`.
Two rules genuinely specific to studios, beyond the mirrored policy:
- **A studio match asserts a second node and an edge.** Confirming an imprint also asserts the network that owns it exists — one lookup yielding two profiles and a `studio_parent` row. This is the whole payoff. The parent is created via `confirmStudio`, already idempotent and non-destructive.
- **The run should report how much future asking it prevented.** `StudioResolution` falls to `.ask` when neither of two offered studios is verified. Every studio confirmed turns some number of those into `.use`, and that is the only tally that says what the run bought rather than what it did.
## Part 3 — The studio profile page
A studio branch in `ProfileGraphHeaderView`, parallel to the existing tag branch — not a new view. Tags already established that seam; a separate view would fork the photo browser, rename, delete and links four ways for one differing block.
- **Suppressed:** gender, hair colour, birth year, career span.
- **Kept:** logo (rounded rect, not a portrait circle), bio, home page and links, AKAs, rating.
- **Added:** the confirmation verdict as a badge — it is the input to `StudioResolution` and already the one fact `StudioGalleryView` surfaces.
- **Added:** the lineage block — parent, sibling imprints, children, each with a video count, each a pivot. Needs `childStudioIds(of:)` lifted out of `studioIdWithDescendants`, and a `videoIds(forStudio:)` that does not yet exist.
- **Changed:** "Co-Actors" reads **Actors** on a studio page. The "Studios" section is dropped — it lists studios *co-occurring on the same videos*, which is largely the two-studio defect; lineage replaces it with the real answer.
With `studio_parent` empty the block must degrade to one honest line — *"No network recorded yet. Match Studios can find it."* — rather than an empty box.
### Part 3b — A network shows its imprints' videos, separated
Added 2026-08-06 on the operator's instruction, reversing decision 4. A merged list would lose exactly the distinction the hierarchy exists to record, so the family view **splits** rather than pools — the same shape as the season-grouped series grid: a collapsible header carrying the studio name and its count, with that studio's grid beneath.
- **`SidebarItem.studioFamily(String)`** — the new case F2 predicted. `.studio` is left exactly as it was, so every existing studio page and saved filter still means what it meant, and the narrower question stays askable.
- **An "Include imprints" toggle** in the lineage block, shown only when the studio actually has imprints — on a leaf it would be a control that visibly does nothing. It flips the pinned selection; the grid owns what it shows.
- **`StudioFamilyGrouping`** in `LibraryCore`, because the ordering and the two-studio rule are decisions. The root leads even when an imprint carries more (it is the page you are on); imprints follow busiest-first, matching the lineage block so the two readings of the hierarchy agree.
- ⚠️ **A two-studio video is filed under the studio that is in this family**, not `studios.first`. Picking blindly would file it under a studio outside the family and drop it from a page it belongs on. It appears once, never once per studio it names.
- ⚠️ **The descendant walk is memoised on the root.** It runs from `recomputeDisplayedAssets`, which fires on every search keystroke — re-walking `studio_parent` each time would put a database read on the typing path.
- Falls back to the studio alone if the graph cannot be read: an empty grid would claim "this network has no videos", which is a stronger and wronger statement than showing only what is certain.

**Suite totals after all of the above:** LibraryCore 1,027 tests, 1 skipped, 0 failures. Plugin repo 129 tests, 4 skipped, 0 failures. macOS and iOS both build.
Two decisions taken while building Part 3, both about keeping the page honest:
- **Video counts come from the ****`studio:`**** TAGS, not from ****`video_studio`****.** The counts sit beside links that pivot the grid, and the grid filters on the string — counting edges would print a number the very next click contradicts. The edge is the better representation; until writes move to it, the display must agree with itself.
- **The header reloads on ****`ReloadAssets`****.** Match All Studios writes `studio_parent` and posts it. Without the subscription, a studio page open at the time keeps reading "no network recorded yet" after the run that recorded one — exactly what that message must never be wrong about.
D9 hygiene gate clean. All fixtures and examples use invented studio names — the gate cannot catch a real one.
⚠️ The plugin is symlinked file-by-file into the app target under `ViLM/LocalPlugins/ActorVideoMetadata/` (gitignored). A new plugin source file needs a symlink added there or the app cannot see it — the build fails with "cannot find X in scope" while the plugin package itself compiles cleanly.
## Corrections from operator testing, 2026-08-06
Three defects found by using the app, kept as corrections rather than quietly fixed — two of them are the same mistake as the one this spec was written to fix, made again in places the spec did not look.
### T1 — 🚨 The batch queue was unusable
A queued studio opened the profile **editor**, copied from how the actor screen hands off. That works for actors only because the operator reaches the candidates *from* the editor, through its Import button — and that sheet searches **people**, so a studio had no route to them at all.
The result: the queue showed the record you already have and never the candidates that caused it to be queued, which is the one question the queue asks. The operator's words: *"I cannot tell what I am looking at as none of the data is right."*
**Fixed** by `StudioMatchReviewView` — a candidate picker showing each candidate with **the network that owns it**, which is the fact that separates two same-named imprints and the whole reason the record was queued. Candidates are passed in from the run rather than re-searched: that request is already paid for, and searching again could return a different answer.
It then shows exactly what would be written, per field. Empty slots tick themselves; anything that would **replace** an existing value starts unticked and names what it would displace. The network is written last, after `confirmStudio` creates it — an edge to a studio with no profile is a dangling parent, one of the defects Studio Health reports. "None of these" records `unmatchable`, which future runs skip.
⚠️ The source's spelling of the name is **shown and never applied**. Renaming a studio moves every video filed under it; that belongs in Repair Tag Spelling.
### T2 — The edit sheet was still the actor form
Same defect as the profile page, one layer down and reached through its own menu: a studio was offered a gender, a hair colour and a birth year. Now hidden for studios, along with the actor-only Import button. Country stays — a studio has one. "Photo Gallery" reads **Logos**, the title reads **Edit Studio**, and the keyboard's next-field chain skips the hidden fields rather than dead-ending on one that is not on screen.
Values already stored in the hidden fields are **preserved, not cleared** — a form that silently nulls what it declines to show is worse than one that shows too much.
### T3 — A missing icon, from an SF Symbol that does not exist
`4 · Match All Studios` had no icon while steps 1–3 did, so the row sat visibly offset. `building.2.crop.circle.badge.checkmark` was invented by analogy with `person.crop.circle.badge.checkmark`, which is real — the building equivalent is not, and **SwiftUI renders a missing symbol as nothing at all** rather than failing.
The same guess had been made a second time, in the Match Studios idle screen. Both fixed, and all **40** symbols across the new screens were then verified to resolve against the system library rather than eyeballed.
### T4 — 🚨 A settled studio stayed on the queue
Operator, 2026-08-06: *"Once I select a studio from the candidate list, the studio is matched and should come off of the list. When I later go look at the studio gallery, I see that it is listed as confirmed."*
The write was correct — the gallery proved it. What was wrong is that the review sheet only **dismissed itself**; it never told the run anything, so the studio stayed under "needs you to choose" for the rest of the session. Settled everywhere except the one screen that had asked the question, which also makes the remaining count untrustworthy.
**Fixed** by having the review report an outcome (`matched` / `ruledOut` / `dismissed`) instead of just closing. A decided studio leaves the queue; closing without deciding keeps it, because nothing was written and it genuinely still needs choosing.
⚠️ **The run's report is not adjusted.** `Confirmed` is what the unattended run did, and folding a hand-made decision into it would credit the run with a choice it explicitly refused to make. What the operator settled is counted separately as **Settled by you**, so the queue shrinking is explained rather than looking like rows going missing.
### T5 — The same defect already existed on the actor run
Found while fixing T4. `VideoBatchMatchModel` has always had `removeFromQueue`; `ActorBatchMatchModel` never did, and `ActorBatchMatchView` only set `reviewing = nil` — so a **matched actor stayed on the "need you to choose" list all session**, exactly as the studio did. Pre-existing, not introduced by this work, and fixed the same way: saving from the queue removes the record.
⚠️ **The three runs still disagree about what a bare dismissal means.** Video clears the row on dismissal (*"you have looked"*); actor and studio now keep it, on the grounds that a record you did not decide about is still undecided. Both are defensible, only one can be right, and this is worth settling — the batch screens were deliberately built alike because *three batch screens that behave differently is three things to learn*.
### T6 — 🚨 The studio provider evicted the actor provider
Operator, 2026-08-06: *"the button to match an actor to the source has disappeared from the actor's edit profile page."*
⚠️ *Named generically here: this page syncs into the PUBLIC repo, where the source must never appear (D9). The concrete type names live in the private plugin repo.*
The source's **studio** provider was given the **actor** provider's plugin id, on the stated reasoning that they are the same source behind the same credential. **`PluginRegistry.register`** keys by `id`, so registering it did not share anything; it **replaced** the actor provider in the registry.
Consequences, only one of which was visible: Import vanished from the actor editor, **and Match All Actors had no provider at all**. A test had even been written asserting the two shared an id — it passed, and it was asserting the bug.
The pattern was already in the codebase and was not followed: the **video** provider carries its own distinct plugin id and expresses the shared account through `credentialId`. **One id per plugin; one credential id per account.** The studio provider now does the same.
Guarded in both repos: the plugin test now asserts the ids differ and the credential ids match, and `PluginRegistryTests` records the eviction behaviour itself so the trap is written down rather than rediscovered.
### T7 — Matching moved to the ellipsis menu
Operator's request, on the same report: put it *"under the ellipsis button like we have done on the video profile page"*. The video inspector carries **Match with …** in its own ellipsis menu rather than inside its edit sheet; the actor profile page now does the same, labelled with the source's own display name so the view never names a source.
Two details: the sheet is handed the **owning library's raw profile**, never the merged cross-library view — saving that back would copy other libraries' fields into the owner. And an accepted canonical rename runs **after** the save, because the rename rewrites the record's identity and a write afterwards would target a row that has just moved.
⚠️ **The editor keeps its own Import button for now.** The actor batch queue hands off to the editor, and that button is how the operator reaches the candidates — removing it would break the actor queue exactly as the studio queue was broken (T1). It should go once the actor run gets its own review sheet like `StudioMatchReviewView`.
### T8 — 🚨 Agreement never confirmed a studio
Operator, 2026-08-06: *"on a number of matched videos, even if the studio name appears on the UI, it isn't recognised as a studio so it doesn't verify — it feels like the data from the website is somehow both right and wrong."*
It is exactly that. `confirmedStudio` required the studio field to be in `accepting` — the studio was verified only when it was **written**. But `changes(for:)` emits **no studio row at all** when the video already carries that studio: agreement produces nothing to accept.
So the source confirming what the library already held wrote nothing, and therefore verified nothing. **The better the data already was, the less likely the studio ever confirmed.** A studio could be correct on every video that credits it and still read "not yet confirmed" forever — and since nothing else confirmed a studio at the time, there was no other route.
Two halves to the fix:
- **Agreement confirms.** A studio the source names that the video already carries is the strongest confirmation available — two independent records agreeing. A studio *offered*, *conflicting*, and *not accepted* still confirms nothing; that rule is untouched.
- ⚠️ **Confirm the spelling the LIBRARY holds, not the source's.** `confirmStudio` keys the profile by name, so confirming "Coast Line" while every video says "CoastLine" would create a confirmed profile nothing points at — the gallery looks up `studio:<tag>` exactly and would still show it unconfirmed. Matched on `StudioResolution.isSameStudio`, so a spacing variant is recognised as the same studio.
The batch path had a second instance: the confirm sat **below** the `guard !fields.isEmpty` early return, so a library with nothing to write skipped it entirely. Moved above, alongside the hierarchy block that had already been moved for the same reason — the comment there described this exact trap and the studio confirm was left behind it.
## Outstanding operator work
63 videos across 31 groupings still carry two studios. These should be resolved through **Fix Duplicate Studios** before Match Studios runs: a video with two studios has no single studio to confirm, and *Connect the Graph* does not go back for what it skipped.
